data.title: US was warned of telecom security risks years before Salt Typhoon
data.description: Nov 19 : The US government was warned in a report it commissioned about major national security risks from weaknesses in the country's telecom networks in 2022, two years before sweeping Chinese-linked cyberespionage known as Salt Typhoon. The report commissioned by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency said US telecommunications networks contained "major structural vulnerabilities" and could be compromised from anywhere in the world. US officials have previously alleged that hackers targeted nine telecom companies, including Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile and Lumen, during the 2024 Salt Typhoon campaign and stole telephone audio intercepts and a large tranche of call-record data. The report, disclosed as part of a lawsuit, has been reviewed by Reuters. Details of the report were first reported by Bloomberg News on Thursday. The June 2022 report described US telecom infrastructure as one in a "perilous and untenable situation," and added that international interconnects could provide attackers with "trusted" access. "The fact that US national networks can be readily compromised from anywhere in the world is not yet widely understood." CISA withheld the report from public release for four years and resisted congressional pressure to publish it, according to Bloomberg News. The agency did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Ron Wyden, a Democratic senator from Oregon, pushed for the release of the report last year. He had said in a statement, "Congress would have had ample time to require mandatory cybersecurity standards for phone companies, in time to prevent the Salt Typhoon hacks" had the report been made public when it was first written.

data.title: Amazon warns NYC delivery bill could add up to $5 per order
data.description: Nov 19 : Amazon said on Thursday legislation being considered by the New York City Council "could add up to $5" to each order, adding that it might be forced to consider moving operations outside the city if the bill passes. • Amazon said in a message to New York City customers that the council is weighing Intro 518, which it said could raise prices and affect how it delivers packages and groceries • The bill, sponsored by Councilmember Tiffany Caban, would require operators of last-mile delivery facilities to be licensed by the city and to directly employ delivery workers rather than contract the work out • Amazon said it works with a network of small delivery businesses and would no longer be able to work with them if the legislation passes • The company said moving operations outside the city would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers • Amazon said it is trying to work with the council and has invited every member to visit its delivery stations, and it has asked customers to contact their council member

data.title: Stocks slip as Anthropic gains on market debut and oil prices rise
data.description: NEW YORK/LONDON, Nov 19 : Global stocks fell on Thursday as US stock traders focused on Anthropic's IPO, while oil prices rose as lingering attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz grabbed market attention. Investors have said that how the first major AI developer to go public trades in the coming days and weeks will be heavily scrutinized to gauge broader sentiment towards AI. The Claude developer's initial public offering was priced at $83 a share, valuing Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion before the stock rose as much as 39 per cent to trade at $115.10 on its debut. "We can't underestimate the importance of this IPO. It sort of serves as a valuation for the wider AI ecosystem," said Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at StoneX. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,011.97 points, or 2.02 per cent, to 49,186.20, the S&P 500 fell 110.35 points, or 1.51 per cent, to 7,213.28 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 351.21 points, or 1.44 per cent, to 24,078.68.  MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 14.30 points, or 1.33 per cent, to 1,060.26. The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.88 per cent, while emerging market stocks fell 20.34 points, or 1.37 per cent, to 1,463.94. Japan's Nikkei rose 419.93 points, or 0.71 per cent, to 59,444.21. The dollar index was steady after its recent rally to 19-month highs lost momentum. "Dollar bulls are going to need more conviction or more bullish news to drive dollar gains in the short run," Shaun Osborne, chief ​currency strategist at Scotiabank, said, pointing to a pickup in risk sentiment linked to Anthropic. The index was little changed at 103.81, with the euro up 0.06 per cent at $1.098. OIL EDGES UP In commodities, oil prices edged higher as renewed attacks in the Strait of Hormuz offset a growing view that the oil market will soon be back in surplus. Iran's navy said in a statement carried by state media that two oil tankers hit naval mines in the waterway and "exploded" on Thursday. Reuters could not independently verify the report. US crude rose 1.24 per cent to $84.29 a barrel and Brent rose to $92.83 per barrel, up 0.96 per cent on the day. Spot gold fell 1.34 per cent to $3,672.67 an ounce and spot silver fell 1.74 per cent to $44.24 an ounce. Copper declined 0.3 per cent to $12,433.00 a ton.

data.title: Ubisoft expects third-quarter net bookings at around €250 million
data.description: Nov 19 : Ubisoft expects net bookings of around 250 million euros ($274.1 million) for the third quarter, the French videogame maker's CFO Frederick Duguet said on Thursday. This reflects a lighter content release program than usual and a particularly competitive holiday season. • Ubisoft's second-quarter net bookings fell 20.8 per cent on the year to 388.9 million euros, but were above its guidance of around 370 million euros, helped by sales of "Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced" • The third phase of its cost-reduction program, targeting a fixed cost base of 1.25 billion euros on a run-rate basis by March 2028, was firmly on track, the company said as it confirmed its full-year targets • Ubisoft expects a "significantly" stronger and diversified content pipeline for fiscal 2027-28 and 2028-29, with releases across major brands • The company expects to return to generating free cash flow and positive non-IFRS EBIT in 2027-28 • "We have established Motherbrain... as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up new possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot said • Ubisoft also cut 166 jobs in Montreal and Quebec City ($1 = 0.91 euros)

data.title: Anthropic hits $2 trillion market value in debut
data.description: NEW YORK, Nov 19 : Anthropic's IPO is having a blockbuster first day following the AI lab's record-setting fundraising. Shares opened more than 30 per cent above their offering price on Thursday at $111.50 a share, conferring a $2 trillion market value - a level exceeded by only a handful of US-listed firms. By reaching that level at the open on Thursday the firm outpaced rival SpaceX, whose value at its opening trade in June hit $1.96 trillion. The company on Wednesday evening priced its offering above range and increased the number of shares being sold, initially valuing the Claude chatbot maker at $1.5 trillion and defying concerns about the state of one of the pillars of the artificial intelligence boom. Shares across the AI sector were mixed as investors sift through worries about the impact of higher rates on a sector that took off during the era of easy money, an age that appears to have come to an end.  MARKET REACTION: US STOCKS: Major indexes were mixed after opening higher, with the Nasdaq <.IXIC> up 0.1 per cent  after rising as much as 2 per cent after the open and the S&P 500 down 0.4 per cent after earlier rising nearly 1 per cent. BONDS: US Treasury yields were little changed, with the 2-year yield flat at 4.8 per cent and the 10-year yield flat at 5.066 per cent. FOREX: The dollar index was off 0.03 per cent at 103.79. COMMENTS: TONY, TRZCINKA, SENIOR PORTFOLIO MANAGER, IMPAX ASSET MANAGEMENT, BOSTON: "The market  is looking through this strong IPO.  It doesn’t settle the concerns driving the de-rating of the trade due to changes at Nvidia, (Democratic) blue wave and sentiment in Washington DC."  MICHAEL ROSEN, CIO, ANGELES INVESTMENTS, SANTA MONICA, CALIFORNIA: “The ANT IPO saw strong demand, giving a near-term boost to sentiment in the AI ecosystem. But it doesn’t change some of the fundamental challenges that have arisen with the departure of Jensen Huang at Nvidia or the political pushback on data center, and AI in general, development.“Demand for computing power remains strong, so this is not an industry in imminent collapse, but there is a realignment of marginal winners and losers among investors, and those with existing computing power in a stronger position than those without. So hyperscalers, with strong balance sheets and cash flows may be better positioned than those more exposed to the pure growth of data center buildout.“We continue to emphasize to investors that historically disruptive technological advances favor those companies that can harness the new technology to create new products and services over those that supply the new technology. Some of those beneficiaries will be existing companies that are most adaptable, but many will be entirely new companies that are being started now or are yet to be born. Investors should alter their investment approach to align with the theme of successfully adapting to this disruptive technology.” TALLEY LEGER, CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST, WEALTH CONSULTING GROUP, KEYPORT, NEW JERSEY: “While Anthropic represents top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure with massive revenue momentum, it isn't a prudent 'buy-at-any-price' opportunity for retail wealth clients . . . We like the enterprise AI narrative, but we do not like overpaying for market sentiment. Patience is a strategy. Let the initial volatility settle, the lock-up period expire, and the company deliver 2–3 quarters of public reporting before establishing a position. . . History shows that retail investors buying hot tech IPOs on day one historically underperform broad market indexes over a 3-year horizon once the initial pop fades.” SHAWN SNYDER, ECONOMIC STRATEGIST, POTOMAC FUND MANAGEMENT, BETHESDA, MARYLAND: “Anthropic’s IPO could provide a much-needed boost to sentiment across the AI ecosystem, as the offering is certainly generating considerable excitement among investors. However, enthusiasm for AI is increasingly competing with concerns about the rising cost of capital, particularly as some Federal Reserve policymakers are discussing the possibility of a 50-basis-point rate hike in December. A successful debut could lift sentiment, though sustaining that enthusiasm may be more difficult.“Over the next 6–12 months, the one indicator we would watch is AI stock market breadth relative to the broader technology sector. The volatility around AI is still frequently described as investor jitters rather than outright fear. In our view, the first sign that AI enthusiasm has peaked may not be a slowdown in AI spending, but the moment investors stop rewarding companies simply for being associated with AI.” MARK HACKETT, CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST, NATIONWIDE FINANCIAL, PHILADELPHIA: “Sentiment and positioning have shifted at a tremendous pace for the AI trade. It is no surprise that Anthropic is highly anticipated, as it is a leader, where the skepticism is more around the more speculative and risky crowd. How the AI space trades today will show if investors are committing new capital or simply reallocating funds from elsewhere. Strength among the competitors and complements would be an encouraging sign that the selloff is near the end, but weakness would tell a different story.” GIL LURIA, HEAD OF TECHNOLOGY RESEARCH, D.A. DAVIDSON, PORTLAND, OREGON: "Anthropic’s IPO is pivotal for the AI investment cycle. A successful IPO could extend the cycle by years and an unsuccessful IPO could stall investment. Indication that the IPO is shaping up well would be very positive for other AI-related stocks." JOE ZIDLE, CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST, CRESSET, NEW YORK: “Landmark IPOs tend to mark turning points in sentiment, so I interpret the success of ANT as an endorsement of the road ahead. Public investors are paying up, and that tells you that the debate has moved from ‘Is this real?’ to ‘Who captures the value?’ That’s a far healthier conversation for the whole AI ecosystem.”

data.title: Musk's SpaceXSI denies liability in UK lawmaker's lawsuit over Grok images
data.description: LONDON, Nov 19 : Elon Musk's SpaceXSI has filed its defence against a British lawmaker's lawsuit over fake images of her created using the Grok AI platform, arguing that obviously fictitious, AI-generated content cannot breach someone's right to privacy. Jess Asato, a member of Britain's governing Labour Party who has publicly criticised both Musk and Grok, is suing after users generated sexualised images of her, including a video of her "being chloroformed and prepared for a sexual assault". In its written defence, dated October 29, SpaceXSI, part of Musk's SpaceX, denies liability for any alleged breach of Asato's privacy or data protection rights. Asato filed her lawsuit at London's High Court for misuse of private information and breaches of data protection laws, alleging the way Grok was designed and trained enabled it to generate sexualised content. The company's defence, in one of the first claims to test liability for the design of an AI system, could provide an insight into how designers may contest similar lawsuits. Lawyers for SpaceX Super Intelligence LLC said it had removed AI-generated images of Asato that breached its terms, including the video depicting Asato being chloroformed. They argued, however, that other images it allowed to remain available "would be understood by reasonable and sensible persons viewing that content to be AI-generated, fictitious and implausible ... rather than as realistic images", meaning Asato has no reasonable expectation of privacy. SpaceXSI also argues it did not breach Asato's data protection rights, including because it "did not determine the content of the relevant users' prompts". LAWMAKER SAYS PLATFORMS SHOULD BE ACCOUNTABLE Asato said in a statement on Thursday that those building powerful AI tools must take responsibility. "SpaceX SI wants to have it both ways," Asato said.  "The company admits it built the AI model, rewrote user requests to add its own graphic details, pulled images from across the internet, and published the results from an account it controls," she said, adding: "Yet it also claims it is a neutral bystander without legal responsibility". Asato is seeking a court order requiring SpaceXSI, which was formerly called xAI and then SpaceXAI, to "implement effective and permanent technical measures" to ensure Grok cannot create manipulated images of her. SpaceXSI says she is not entitled to such an order.  Grok, which is distributed through social media platform X, is subject to regulatory probes in several countries after an outcry over its use to create non-consensual sexualised images. In mid-January, xAI said it restricted image editing in Grok and blocked users from generating images of people in revealing clothing "where it's illegal".  But Reuters found in early February that, even after new curbs, Grok continued to generate sexualised images of people even when users explicitly warned the subjects did not consent. X and xAI did not address detailed questions from Reuters about Grok's generation of sexualised material. In July, xAI sued a man in the US alleging he misused Grok to create child sexual abuse material, in one of the first cases of its kind brought by an AI company.

data.title: Take-Two set to shatter sales records as 'GTA VI' launches to massive fanfare
data.description: Nov 19 : Criminal duo Lucia and Jason's blitz through Vice City in "GTA VI" is set to help Take-Two Interactive — the publisher of the blockbuster game that is now a global cultural phenomenon — rake in nearly $2 billion in estimated first-day sales. Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of GTA developer Rockstar Games, is not a household name despite its portfolio of massive hits including the "Red Dead Redemption" franchise and the "NBA 2K" basketball series. Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimates total units sold at 19.1 million as of Thursday morning, translating to about $1.84 billion in revenue for Take-Two. That is more than twice the roughly $800 million worth of copies GTA V sold on its first day in 2013, widely regarded as the best-selling videogame in the first 24 hours. Meanwhile, Take-Two has remained tight-lipped about GTA VI demand since it opened for pre-orders in June, limiting commentary to saying demand has been "unprecedented" or "far exceeding expectations." "The title is so widely anticipated, consumers appear very, very excited, and all the press so far has been universally positive, but we still aren't ready to declare victory," CEO Strauss Zelnick said on Take-Two's earnings call earlier this month. "We tend to avoid claiming success before it occurs." Take-Two shares were down about 1 per cent on Thursday after closing 6 per cent higher in the previous session. GTA VI MARKETING BLITZ Take-Two has shelled out an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs for GTA VI, making it one of the most expensive entertainment projects. Sensor Tower estimates that the game's promotional trailer, GTA VI "Extended Look", on Netflix in August helped drive a sixfold jump in pre-orders. In Miami — which Vice City is based on — the city's NBA team celebrated the release on Wednesday with a Vice City-themed match. Over the weekend, the company is hosting "GTA VI: The Festival" — a music show with a star-studded line-up that includes Grammy-winning rapper Cardi B, hip hop record producer Metro Boomin and rapper Travis Scott. WHAT NEXT FOR TAKE-TWO? Investors have been waiting to hear from Take-Two about its plans for a PC launch of GTA VI and an online version rollout. The online, multiplayer component of a videogame is crucial in turning the title into a recurring revenue engine. Some industry analysts are expecting the PC launch and online mode in 2027. Brokerage TD Cowen named Take-Two one of its 'Best Ideas' for 2027, with its analyst Doug Creutz upbeat about the company's financial prospects when the game releases online. "The potential ceiling for GTA VI's long-term recurrent consumer spending performance is very high ... 'when' and 'how big' the next GTA Online will be is the most important question for the stock, more so than GTA VI unit sales."

data.title: Anthropic draws bullish Wall Street calls ahead of Nasdaq debut
data.description: Nov 19 : Ahead of Anthropic's blockbuster market debut, brokerages including Needham and Melius Research started coverage of the AI firm with bullish recommendations, betting the company would emerge as the "real AI disruptor". Anthropic was on course to secure a $1.9 trillion valuation when its shares start trading on Thursday. The stock was set to open at $105, 26.5 per cent higher than the IPO price of $83 per share, according to indications as of 10.45 am ET. Feverish demand for Anthropic shares amid a broader tech selloff, underscores enduring investor appetite for pure AI plays after enthusiasm for the sector softened in recent weeks. "Anthropic maybe one of the few AI stocks that holds up in the near term, while the rest of the AI trade still faces questions," said Ben Reitzes, analyst at Melius Research, as he started coverage on the stock with a "buy" rating and a 24-month price target of $155. Melius' target, the highest so far among analysts that have launched coverage, implies an upside of nearly 87 per cent from Anthropic's IPO price. "Growth opportunities like Anthropic rarely come along, but we think history puts Anthropic in the same dominant bucket as fellow tech titans Amazon, Google and Microsoft," Needham said, as it started coverage with a "buy" rating and a $150 price target. Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google. Both Melius and Citizens, which started coverage with a "market outperform" rating and a $125 price target, expect the firm's revenues to hit over $400 billion by 2029. A syndicate of more than 20 banks was involved in the IPO, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley working as the lead underwriters. data.title: NASA confirms Voyager 1 probe's 'light-day' distance milestone
data.description: WASHINGTON, Nov 19 : NASA confirmed on Thursday that its Voyager 1 probe has achieved an unprecedented distance milestone — the first spacecraft to travel beyond a light-day from Earth — while flying into an uncertain future in interstellar space. The US space agency said it received a radio signal from the robotic explorer, launched in 1977, indicating that it passed the distance that light travels in 24 hours — about 16 billion miles (26 billion km) — as expected on Wednesday at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object. NASA waited a day to make the official announcement because it took about that long for the spacecraft's signal to reach Earth. "Traveling a light-day is a singular feat for a spacecraft, but Voyager is so much more than a distant traveler. The Voyager mission would be remarkable just for what it contributed to planetary science with the Grand Tour of the outer planets," Joe Westlake, director of NASA's heliophysics division, said in a statement released by the agency. "But it went on to become central to NASA's fleet of heliophysics missions offering insights into the star that we all revolve around, the sun," Westlake said. Voyager 1 journeyed past Jupiter and Saturn, the solar system's two largest planets, earlier in its mission. It continues to gather scientific data. Voyager 1 is flying at almost 38,000 miles per hour (61,000 kph). It crossed the outer edge of the heliosphere, a protective bubble of particles and magnetic fields produced by the sun, to enter ‌interstellar space ⁠in 2012. Its twin, Voyager 2, was also launched in 1977 and entered interstellar space in 2018. A representative at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory said this week that recent power-saving measures could give the two Voyager spacecraft enough power to stay in communication with Earth for three to four more years. Voyager 1 is still collecting data in the near-vacuum of interstellar space on effects from the sun such as solar storms that cause shocks and pressure fronts that extend as far away as the probe's current location. The 50th anniversary of its launch is next year.

data.title: Palo Alto's raised sales forecast powers rally in cybersecurity stocks
data.description: Nov 19 : Palo Alto Networks shares gained more than 6 per cent on Thursday as its higher annual forecast lifted cybersecurity stocks, with investors betting companies would spend big on defending against sophisticated AI-enabled cyberattacks. If the gains hold, Palo Alto would add more than $18 billion to its market value. Investor interest in cybersecurity firms has grown as AI reshapes the cyber arms race — the technology helps attackers uncover and exploit vulnerabilities faster, while increasing demand for software that can identify, block and respond to emerging threats before they multiply. Those concerns have been reinforced by a series of recent technology outages and vulnerabilities identified in Java and PHP, two programming languages underpinning millions of business applications and websites. "As companies accelerate AI adoption, cybersecurity is becoming an increasingly mission-critical, non-discretionary investment," said Ivan Feinseth, director of research at Tigress Financial Partners. At least 20 brokerages raised their price targets on Palo Alto after its earnings report, giving it a median price target of $425, according to data compiled by LSEG. The upbeat forecast from the company, which also announced a $4.5 billion acquisition of AI startup Applied Compute on Wednesday, boosted sentiment across the cybersecurity sector. Shares of CrowdStrike, Zscaler and Fortinet climbed between 2 per cent and 9 per cent, while Okta, Cloudflare, F5 and SentinelOne gained 1 per cent to 10 per cent each, extending the sector's rally. Technology stocks were also rising ahead of Anthropic's market debut later on Thursday. The Claude maker priced the largest initial public offering on record above its marketed range, helping lift the Nasdaq composite about 2 per cent and reviving appetite for beaten-down AI-linked stocks.

data.title: Anthropic set to secure $1.8 trillion valuation in strong Nasdaq debut
data.description: Nov 19 : Anthropic was on course to secure a $1.8 trillion valuation when its shares start trading on Thursday, in a historic debut that pits promises of AI as an economic game-changer against fears of a market bubble and risks to humanity. The stock was set to open at $99.82, about 20 per cent higher than the IPO price of $83, according to indications as of 9.50 am ET. The Claude chatbot maker's upsized IPO, together with Tuesday's earnings report by AI poster child Nvidia, signals the industry has nominally passed the two big tests facing it this week. The strong demand for Anthropic shares amid a broader tech selloff offers hope to a sector where euphoria has somewhat cooled in recent weeks. "I've looked at this whole week as a referendum on AI. Nvidia gave us a read on the buildout, and Anthropic is about to give us a read on investor appetite for the next generation of AI companies," Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion, said before the Anthropic debut. AI technology has boosted economic growth, sparked doomsday warnings and arguably helped usher in a data-center-skeptic Democratic tsunami in the US midterm elections. Investors who once embraced the boom have turned skeptical in recent weeks over concerns that the enormous spending needed to build out the sector and the mounting debt loads may not be justified by the eventual returns. AN INDUSTRY BENCHMARK As the first frontier AI company to go public, Anthropic is poised to become the sector's benchmark, with its arch-rival OpenAI reportedly eyeing a 2027 listing. The company sold 980 million shares at $83 each, pricing the IPO above its initial range of $70 to $78 set when it launched the road show. Its IPO proceeds could climb to as much as $93.5 billion if underwriters fully exercise their option to purchase additional shares. Currently, the figure sits at over $107 billion, including the additional $26 billion raised through a private placement. AMD, Broadcom, Alphabet's Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC were the investors in the private placement. "Some of the demand may simply reflect investors not wanting to miss out on the rare opportunity to gain exposure to a leading AI company, even if its long-term profitability remains uncertain," IPOX associate Lukas Muehlbauer said. London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates passive demand from index-tracking funds will account for purchase of up to 30 per cent of Anthropic's shares offered by the end of the year. Anthropic will also join the trillion-dollar club stacked with behemoths such as Microsoft, Apple and Nvidia. The blockbuster deal is going to earn the underwriters, led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, a $550 million fee, a regulatory filing showed. BIG PAYDAY FOR CO-FOUNDERS Although shares can be volatile in the days following a listing, Anthropic's IPO is set to create thousands of paper millionaires and a handful of billionaires. Based on the IPO price, CEO Dario Amodei and his six co-founders, who together own about 10 per cent of the company, had stakes valued at nearly $150 billion, according to a Reuters calculation based on details in the filing. More broadly, the listing is expected to create a wave of new wealth across the AI sector, rewarding everyone from early researchers and engineers to administrative staff. JUSTIFYING THE PRICE TAG Debate has intensified across global markets in recent months over whether the AI boom is veering into bubble territory, with economists, CEOs and political leaders split over its sustainability. Much of the scrutiny has focused on circular financing arrangements. A complicated web of deals between AI companies, chipmakers, cloud providers and investors has raised questions over how much of the industry's growth is being fueled by money circulating within the same ecosystem. Anthropic's breakneck growth has so far defied these concerns, but some investors have said they may wait for the initial euphoria to subside before buying. "Anthropic is a one-trick pony. People compare it with Amazon because even Amazon lost money for several years, but Anthropic won't have that luxury," said Bill Gunderson, partner at GCG Advisory Partners. "They've got to get to profitability soon." Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google, underscoring how its rapid growth hinges on securing vast amounts of future computing capacity, some of which relies on financing beyond the company's control. Investors will be watching Anthropic's debut and subsequent trading closely, with analysts expecting the stock to emerge as a proxy for the broader AI trade. The company will also need to balance growth with calls to slow the development of advanced AI models. Anthropic warned in its IPO prospectus that AI could behave unpredictably and advance faster than oversight mechanisms.

data.title: Dollar takes a breather as investors eye Anthropic IPO
data.description: NEW YORK, Nov 19 : The dollar eased against most major peers on Thursday as its recent rally lost momentum ahead of AI company Anthropic's market debut, seen as a key test of appetite for riskier assets and broader market sentiment. The dollar rally started on November 10 when hotter-than-expected US inflation data bolstered expectations that the US Federal Reserve would tighten its policy.  Fed Governor Christopher Waller called for a more aggressive response to inflation, while minutes of the central bank's October 27 to 28 meeting showed policymakers increasingly concerned that additional tightening might be needed.  "The dollar has had a good run here ... I think a lot of good news is priced into the dollar at this point," Shaun Osborne, chief ​currency strategist at Scotiabank, said. "Dollar bulls are going to need more conviction or more bullish news to drive dollar gains in the short run here," said Osborne, who pegged some of the dollar's softer tone to a pickup in risk sentiment ahead of the Anthropic IPO. Nasdaq futures rose on Thursday after Anthropic priced its IPO above the marketed range, bolstering expectations for a strong debut and reviving sentiment around AI stocks. The dollar index this week reached its highest level since April 2, 2025, when US President Donald Trump revealed a sweeping tariff package, triggering a selloff in US assets.  It was last down 0.2 per cent at 103.65, after reaching 103.97. The euro rose 0.2 per cent to $1.1002. Barclays analysts said fiscal stimulus and strong AI-related capital spending point to a resilient US economy, a wider output gap and higher-for-longer interest rates, all supportive of dollar strength. The dollar's gains have come despite a selloff in technology shares. A Deutsche Bank tracker following more than 100 foreign-domiciled exchange-traded funds showed large dip-buying of US stocks by foreigners over the last two weeks, the biggest buying spree so far this year. Such a move reinforces the view that the dollar has been supported by investor flows into US equities. YEN SLIPS AS SAFE-HAVEN FLOWS FADE The dollar was up 0.4 per cent to 159.905 yen, snapping a four-day losing streak. Analysts said that a further selloff in AI-linked assets could support the yen through safe-haven buying and repatriation flows, with the impact likely to be more pronounced against other currencies than against the dollar. The risk-sensitive Aussie was about flat on the day after hitting a fresh 11-month low earlier in the session. Australia's employment fell for a second straight month in October and the jobless rate climbed to a five-year high, bolstering the view that rates have likely peaked. "The sharp hawkish repricing of Fed rate hike expectations is contributing (to) the weakness in commodity prices and related currencies," said Lee Hardman, senior currency analyst at MUFG. UBS brought forward its forecast for the first Reserve Bank of Australia rate cut to August next year from November, and extended the easing cycle to three cuts from two, citing elevated inflation and a deterioration in the labour and housing markets. Sterling pulled back from a 20-month high against the euro, though investors remained upbeat about the UK interest rate outlook and wary of headwinds facing the single currency ahead of key elections across Europe in 2027. The pound rose 0.1 per cent against the dollar to $1.3162. In cryptocurrency markets, bitcoin rose 2.5 per cent to $63,870, pulling away from the four-month low of $62,026 touched on Sunday, aided by stronger risk appetite.
